title: Malayalam language and alphabet
at_a_glance: Language family: Dravidian, Southern Dravidian, Tamil-Kannada, Tamil-Kodagu, Tamil-Malayalam
notable_features: Type of writing system: Abugida / Syllabic Alphabet in which all consonants have an inherent vowel. Diacritics, which can appear above, below, before or after a consonant, are used to change the inherent vowel.
When they appear at the beginning of a syllable, vowels are written as independent letters.
When certain consonants occur together, special conjunct symbols are used which combine the essential parts of each letter.
Writing direction: left to right in horizontal lines.
Used to write: Kodava, Konkani, Malayalam, Ravula
